text.p: - Chechen rebel leader Shamil Basayev says he is ready to shake hands with Boris Yeltsin if the Russian president appologises to the Chechen people.
- The cash-strapped fleet of Russian nuclear ice-breakers could have a bright future once it finds its place in the market economy.
- Russia may soon sharply cut alcohol imports and introduce state monopoly on strong spirits.
- Russian customs committee and the tax service could eventually become part of the finance ministry.
- President Boris Yeltsin will personally chair a meeting supposed to tackle the problem of the country's crippled pension fund.
- Earl Edwin Pitts, an FBI agent arrested in the US on charges of spying for Russia, has fallen victim to confessions of a former Russian UN worker.
